Construction of epidemics
=========================
Parameters: initial state and duration
--------------------------------------
```{julia}
#| label: parameters
const duration   = 15 ;
const MAXPOP     = 20 ;
const initial    = SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0) ;
const population = 5 ;
```

Here are useful abbreviations for some imports from `EpidemicsCFTP`:
```{julia}
#| echo: false
labels   = [:AI  :AIF :I  :P  :R  :C]
import EpidemicsCFTP: AI, AIF, I, P, R, C
pretty_table(map(eval, labels), header=vec(labels), alignment = :l)
```

`EpidemicsUtilities` supplies some constants 
used for the plotting parameter `select`, namely
```{julia}
import EpidemicsUtilities: ACTIVATED, REGIONS, BOUNDARIES, BASIC, 
                        ELEMENTS, LFE, LFET, LFER, MOST, NFZ
```

Unconditioned epidemic
----------------------

We work with an `Innovation`, used to generate an `Evolution` for an unconditioned 
epidemic.
Construct an `Innovation` and a corresponding `Evolution` as follows.
```{julia}
infections = AIF[I(2.0,1,2), I(2.5,3,4), I(3.0,1,3), I(4.0,2,5), I(4.5,2,3), 
        I(5.0,2,4), I(5.5,3,4), I(6.0,2,3), I(10.0,4,5), I(11.0,4,5)]
removals   = R[R(0.5,3), R(1.0,5), R(2.0,4), R(7.0,5)]
cremovals  = C[C(3.5,1), C(6.5,4), C(8.0,3), C(12.0,5), C(13.0,5)]
uiv1 = Innovation(population, infections, removals ∪ map(R, cremovals))
```
The `Evolution` of the corresponding  (_unconditioned_) epidemic is:
```{julia}
uev1 = Evolution(initial, uiv1)
```

Note that we have not added any removals which would turn out to sit
on the removed portion of their timeline, since these will not be activated
nor influence dynamics under updating of the epidemic conditional on
prescribed removals.

Here is a table of the evolution of the epidemic:

```{julia}
#| echo: false 
uflow = table_trajectories1(duration, uev1.trajectory) ;
header = [:t, :susceptibles, :infectives, :removals, :epidemic]
Markdown.parse(pretty_table(String, uflow[:,header], 
  header=header, tf=tf_markdown, alignment=[:l, :c, :c, :c, :c]))
```


{{< pagebreak >}}


Draft of Figure 3 [@ConnorKendall-2023]
=======================================
We first graph the generating incidents corresponding to the unconditional epidemic (`uev1`).

**Caption in draft paper:** 
"Graphical representation of unconditioned \(\SIR\) epidemic. There are five time-lines."

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-figure-3-0
#| fig-cap: "`[figure-3-0.pdf]` Infections are denoted by light orange       \
#|           circles, with arrows pointing upwards to target; removals are   \
#|           denoted by light brown circles                                  \
#|           [Figure 3a, @ConnorKendall-2023]." 
axes_plot = plot(uflow, yintercept=1:initial.n,
    Geom.hline(style=:dash, size=0.1mm, color=theme.scaffold),
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=initial.n + 0.25),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    style(default_color=theme.background),
    Theme(
        panel_fill=theme.blank,
        default_color=theme.default,
        background_color=theme.background,
        major_label_font="CMU Serif",   minor_label_font="CMU Serif",
        minor_label_color=theme.legend, major_label_color=theme.legend,
        major_label_font_size=8pt,      minor_label_font_size=6pt,
        grid_line_width=0mm,
)) ;

push!(axes_plot, layer(uflow, x=:t, y=:empty, Geom.line,
    style(line_width=2theme.trail, default_color=theme.scaffold))) ;

lines_plot = new_figure(axes_plot,
    Scale.y_continuous(labels=(initial.n ≤ EpidemicsUtilities.MAXPOP ?
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_circled(i; n=initial.n) :
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_bracketed(i; n=initial.n))),
    Guide.yticks(ticks=collect(1:(initial.n))),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines")) ;

depict("figure-3-0", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), uev1, duration, theme=theme, 
        select=ELEMENTS),
        title="Incidents determining the unconditioned epidemic"),
    figdir="Figure"
)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-figure-3-1
#| fig-cap: "`[figure-3-1.pdf]` Infections (orange circles) in the           \
#|           unconditioned epidemic are realised whenever an infection       \
#|           target is the least uninfected timeline at the relevant time.   \
#|           Removals (light brown circles) are realized whenever they       \
#|           occur in the infected region; if so then the lowest infected    \
#|           timeline incurs a removal, indicated by a purple disk if        \
#|           not coincident with the generating removal incident             \
#|           [Figure 3b, @ConnorKendall-2023]." 
depict("figure-3-1", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), uev1, duration, theme=theme, 
        select=MOST),
        title="Evolution of the unconditioned epidemic"),
    figdir="Figure"
)
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

Draft of Figure 4 [@ConnorKendall-2023]
=======================================
We now graph the generating incidents corresponding to a conditional form of the epidemic (`cev1`).

**Caption in draft paper:** 
"Illustration of no-fly zone, epidemic trajectory and last-viable epidemic for this graphical representation."

We construct an adapted `Innovation` and a corresponding `CEvolution` as follows.
The No-Fly Zone (NFZ) and Last Feasible Epidemic (LFE) are computed
based on the supplied `Innovation` (it would normally computed as part of an
update of the `CEvolution` using a further `Innovation`). The logic of the
accept/reject constituent of the updating procedure is that LFE infections are
retained in the update unless superseded by a new and viable subsequent
infection supplied
by the further `Innovation`. Additionally new and viable 
infections are discarded if otherwise they would infect the NFZ, since otherwise they would trigger activation of a removal which had not been conditioned to occur.

```{julia}
civ1 = Innovation(population, infections, removals, cremovals)
cevx = CEvolution(initial, civ1)
cev1 = CEvolution(cevx, civ1)
```

Table of various aspects of the epidemic:
```{julia}
#| echo: false
cev  = cev1
traj = [0.0] ∪ [x.t for x in cev.history if x isa AIF]
jumps = [0.0] ∪ [z.t for z in cev.LFE if z isa AIF]
pretty_table(
    vcat(transpose(cev.NFZ), transpose(traj), transpose(jumps)),
    header=[n for n in range(1,length(traj))],
    row_labels=["NFZ terminus time", "Infection time", "LFE infection time"],
    row_label_column_title="Timeline"
    )
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-figure-4
#| fig-cap: "`[figure-4.pdf]` The conditional epidemic evolution is           \
#|           accompanied here by the Last Feasible Epidemic (the red          \
#|           _slowest_ epidemic which does not violate constraints imposed by \
#|           conditioned removals); the No-Fly Zone (the blue-grey region     \
#|           which must not be infected if the _unconditioned_ removals are   \      
#|           not to be activated). These are relevant when seeking to update  \
#|           the current evolution, though both are recomputed using new      \
#|           removals and infections working recursively from the right.      \
#|           [Figure 4, @ConnorKendall-2023]."
depict("figure-4", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), cev1, duration, theme=theme, 
        select=MOST | LFE | NFZ),
        title="Conditioned epidemic with Last Feasible Epidemic and No-Fly Zone"),
    figdir="Figure"
)
```

Note that NFZ and LFE are calculated anew at each update, _after_ updating the CRemoval marks and re-sampling the non-activated Removals.
They summarize recursive calculations, running backwards in process time, aimed at determining whether
new infections should be allowed to proceed. (LFE applies to infections targetting at or below epidemic trajectory;
NFZ to infections targetting above epidemic trajectory.)




{{< pagebreak >}}

Draft of Figure 5 [@ConnorKendall-2023]
=======================================
**Caption in draft paper:**
Demonstration of the update of removals, beginning from the realisation in [the previous] Figure.

We now consider the effect of updating the removals.

```{julia}
#infections = AIF[I(2.0,1,2), I(2.5,3,4), I(3.0,1,3), I(4.0,2,5), I(5.0,2,4),
#        I(5.5,3,4), I(6.0,2,3), I(10.0,4,5), I(11.0,4,5)]
newremovals   = R[R(0.8,2), R(1.5,3), R(3.2,4), R(6.0,5), R(8.5,5)]
newcremovals  = C[C(3.5,3), C(6.5,3), C(8.0,4), C(12.0,5), C(13.0,5)]
civ2a      = Innovation(population, infections, newremovals, newcremovals)
cev2x      = CEvolution(initial, civ2a)
cev2       = CEvolution(cev2x, civ2a) ;
```



Table of various aspects of the epidemic:
```{julia}
#| echo: false
cev  = cev2
traj = [0.0] ∪ [x.t for x in cev.history if x isa AIF]
jumps = [0.0] ∪ [z.t for z in cev.LFE if z isa AIF]
pretty_table(
    vcat(transpose(cev.NFZ), transpose(traj), transpose(jumps)),
    header=[n for n in range(1,length(traj))],
    row_labels=["NFZ terminus time", "Infection time", "LFE infection time"],
    row_label_column_title="Timeline"
    )
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-figure-5
#| fig-cap: "`[figure-5.pdf]` The conditional epidemic evolution is           \
#|           now updated by removing (inactivated) Removals and updating      \
#|            targets of some CRemovals                                       \
#|           [Figure 5, @ConnorKendall-2023]."
depict("figure-5", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), cev2, duration, theme=theme, 
        select=MOST | LFE | NFZ),
        title="Conditioned epidemic with Removals and CRemovals updated"),
    figdir="Figure"
)
```


{{< pagebreak >}}


Draft of Figure 6 [@ConnorKendall-2023]
=======================================
**Caption in draft paper:**
Demonstration of the update of infections (the right-most figure (b)), 
beginning from the realisation in [the previous] Figure.

Finally we update the infections.
```{julia}
perpetuated    = [P(10.00,4,5), P(5.00,2,4), P(3.00,1,3), P(2.00,1,2)]
new_infections = [I(9.00,4,5), I(7.20,4,5), I(7.00,3,4), I(4.20,3,4),
    I(2.20,4,5), I(1.50,1,2), I(1.00,2,3), I(0.50,1,2)]

civ3 = Innovation(population, new_infections, newremovals, newcremovals)
cev3 = CEvolution(cev2, civ3) ;
```

Table of various aspects of the epidemic:
```{julia}
#| echo: false
cev  = cev3
traj = [0.0] ∪ [x.t for x in cev.history if x isa AIF]
jumps = [0.0] ∪ [z.t for z in cev.LFE if z isa AIF]
pretty_table(
    vcat(transpose(cev.NFZ), transpose(traj), transpose(jumps)),
    header=[n for n in range(1,length(traj))],
    row_labels=["NFZ terminus time", "Infection time", "LFE infection time"],
    row_label_column_title="Timeline"
    )
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-figure-6
#| fig-cap: "`[figure-6.pdf]` The conditional epidemic evolution is           \
#|           completed by proposing new infections (some old infections       \
#|           perpetuated, some new infections violate NFZ so not admitted)    \
#|           [Figure 6, @ConnorKendall-2023]."
depict("figure-6", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), cev3, duration, theme=theme, 
        select=MOST | LFE | NFZ),
        title="Conditioned epidemic with Infections updated"),
    figdir="Figure"
)
```


{{< pagebreak >}}


Draft of Figure 7 [@ConnorKendall-2023]
=======================================
CFTP depends on examination of updates started at maximal ("fast") and minimal ("slow") states,
which we illustrate here.

**Caption in draft paper:** 
"Representation of fastest and slowest states, \(E^\text{fast}\) and \(E^\text{slow}\)."

Here it is useful to ensure the correct well-ordering of the set of all incidents
(ordering first by time, and then by ensuring that infections have priority over removals).


```{julia}
#| include: false
theme = create_theme(load_theme("config/test-theme.yml"))

set_default_plot_size(theme.figwidth, theme.figheight)
```

```{julia}
cremovaltimes = [x.t for x in cremovals]
cevslowest    = extremal_evolution(initial, duration, cremovaltimes, maximal=false) ;
cevfastest    = extremal_evolution(initial, duration, cremovaltimes, maximal=true) ;
```

::: {#fig-figure-7 layout-ncol=2}


```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-figure-7a
#| fig-cap: "`[figure-7a.pdf]` The fastest conditional epidemic evolution is   \
#|           constructed by infecting all timelines immediately                \
#|           [Figure 7(a), @ConnorKendall-2023]."
depict("figure-7a", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), cevfastest, duration, theme=theme, 
        select=BOUNDARIES | BASIC),
        title="Fastest conditioned epidemic"),
    figdir="Figure"
)
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-figure-7b
#| fig-cap: "`[figure-7b.pdf]` The slowest conditional epidemic evolution is   \
#|           constructed by infecting all timelines as late as is compatible   \
#|           with conditioning on observed removals                            \
#|           [Figure 7(b), @ConnorKendall-2023]."
depict("figure-7b", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), cevslowest, duration, theme=theme, 
        select=BOUNDARIES | BASIC),
        title="Slowest conditioned epidemic"),
    figdir="Figure"
)
```

:::


Figure 7(a): fastest state \(E^\text{fast}\):
: In the fastest state the epidemic proceeds at the fastest possible speed,
so all timelines are infected immediately.

Figure 7(b): slowest state \(E^\text{slow}\):
: In the slowest
state the epidemic proceeds at the slowest possible speed compatible with all conditioned removals
actually happening.



{{< pagebreak >}}

Draft of Figure 8 [@ConnorKendall-2023]
=======================================
We need to exhibit a set \(F_\delta\) which 
possesses certain properties with respect to the update process.

**Caption in draft paper:** 
"Example of an epidemic belonging to the set \(F_\delta\)."

```{julia}
#| include: false
theme = create_theme(load_theme("config/theme.yml"))

set_default_plot_size(theme.figwidth, theme.figheight)
```

We produce an example by setting relevant infections to occur
in order on or before a fixed small time \(\delta>0\) smaller than
any of the conditioned removal times (here we set \(\delta=3.0\)).

```{julia}
infectionssmall = [I(k*0.6, k, k+1) for k in range(1, population-1)]
removalssmall   = [R(k*0.1-0.05, k+1) for k in range(1, population-1)]
civsmall = Innovation(population, infectionssmall, removalssmall, cremovals)
cevsmall = Evolution(initial, civsmall)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-figure-8
#| fig-cap: "`[figure-8.pdf]` A conditional epidemic in which all \
#|           activated infections occur before time 3.0,          \
#|           before smallest observed removal time.               \
#|           [Figure 8, @ConnorKendall-2023]."
depict("figure-8", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), cevsmall, duration, theme=theme, 
        select=BOUNDARIES | BASIC),
        title="Conditioned epidemic from a given small set."),
    figdir="Figure"
)
```
